question: What does drug non-compliance mean in patient care?

options.A: Storing drugs in improper temperature conditions
options.B: Reporting mild side effects to the doctor
options.C: Failing to follow a prescribed medication regimen
options.D: Buying medications from unregistered local markets

explanation: Non-compliance represents any deviation from the agreed treatment plan set by the healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: A patient stops taking antihypertensive drugs because they feel fine. What is this action considered?
explanation: When a patient deliberately decides to stop medication based on personal judgment, it constitutes intentional non-compliance. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: The main cause of medication non-adherence related to pill burden is...

options.A: Taking drugs exclusively on an empty stomach
options.D: Complex dosing schedules throughout the day

explanation: Managing multiple medications with different timings often overwhelms patients, leading to missed doses. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do unpleasant side effects often lead directly to drug non-compliance?

options.A: Pharmacies stop stocking medications causing mild reactions
options.B: Patients stop taking the drug to avoid discomfort
options.C: Metabolic pathways destroy the active drug ingredients
options.D: Body weight increases rapidly during adverse reactions

explanation: Unmanaged side effects make patients associate the treatment with suffering rather than healing, causing them to quit. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h2)

question: Uncontrolled hypertension resulting from missed medication doses primarily damages...

options.B: Skeletal muscles in the lower limbs
options.C: Target organs like the heart and kidneys

explanation: Persistent high blood pressure places excessive strain on delicate blood vessels supplying vital organs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h3)

question: A diabetic patient experiences worsening neuropathy due to erratic drug adherence. What is the primary reason for this decline?

options.A: Intermittent drug levels fail to maintain stable blood glucose control
options.B: Nerve cells develop a sudden allergy to glucose
options.C: Oral hypoglycemic agents lose potency in tropical climates
options.D: The pancreas completely stops producing insulin overnight

explanation: Inconsistent medication causes fluctuations in blood sugar that gradually injure peripheral nerves over time. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of stopping antibiotic therapy prematurely?

options.A: Rapid increase in red blood cell production
options.B: Permanent immunity against all future infections
options.C: Immediate complete cure of the bacterial infection

explanation: Incomplete courses leave behind the strongest microbes, which then multiply and resist standard treatments. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do resistant infections often require more expensive secondary medications?

options.A: Nurses must administer reserve drugs through specialized pumps
options.B: First-line drugs can no longer kill the mutated microorganisms
options.C: Patients refuse to swallow standard tablets
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies inflate prices for chronic disease drugs

explanation: When standard antimicrobial agents fail due to resistance, clinicians must rely on alternative drugs that are frequently costlier and harder to source. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h4)

question: What happens when a patient takes extra medication to make up for a missed dose?

options.A: The body rapidly metabolizes excess ingredients
options.D: Risk of acute drug toxicity increases

explanation: Taking extra pills concentrates the drug in the bloodstream beyond safe therapeutic thresholds, causing toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which nursing action prevents medication toxicity related to dose adjustments?

options.A: Recommending double doses whenever symptoms worsen
options.B: Advise patients to stop all drugs if one dose is missed
options.C: Instructing patients never to double up on missed doses
options.D: Encouraging patients to buy cheaper herbal alternatives

explanation: Clear guidance on handling missed doses protects patients from accidental over-medication and dangerous side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: A major economic consequence of widespread medication non-compliance is...

options.A: Lower operational costs for local pharmacies
options.B: Surplus funding within government health budgets
options.C: Increased hospital admissions and emergency visits
options.D: Decreased demand for specialized nursing staff

explanation: Unmanaged diseases inevitably deteriorate, forcing patients to seek costly emergency and inpatient care. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: How does patient non-compliance affect household finances in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Insurance companies automatically cover all unplanned treatments
options.B: Repeated disease relapses drain savings through emergency care costs
options.C: Families save money by reducing daily pharmaceutical purchases
options.D: Employers provide full financial support for chronic illnesses

explanation: Treating advanced complications is far more expensive than maintaining regular medication, depleting family finances. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is a reliable objective method for a nurse to assess medication adherence?

options.B: Reviewing general dietary habits at home
options.C: Conducting pill counts during clinic visits
options.D: Asking if the patient remembers taking drugs

explanation: Counting remaining pills in the container provides concrete physical evidence of whether medications are being taken. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why should nurses use non-judgmental language when asking about missed doses?

options.A: To ensure the pharmacy refills drugs without delay
options.B: To prevent the doctor from changing the prescription
options.C: To comply with hospital billing regulations
options.D: To encourage the patient to give an honest answer

explanation: Patients hide non-compliance if they fear scolding or punishment from healthcare personnel. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which tool is most practical to help elderly patients manage multiple daily pills?

options.B: Weekly text messages from the hospital
options.C: Large glass storage jars for all tablets

explanation: Compartmentalized pill boxes allow patients to see at a glance whether they have taken their scheduled doses. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h8)
